documents.abstract: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.

Hybrid work has moved from an emergency response to a deliberate work-design option, but its productivity consequences depend on how flexibility and digital coordination are organized. This study examined the relationship between hybrid work model and employee productivity in civil society organizations in Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the relationship between work-location flexibility and employee productivity and determined the relationship between digital collaboration effectiveness and employee productivity. A survey research design was adopted. The study covered eight selected civil society organizations, with a population of 267 employees whose roles were compatible with hybrid work. A sample of 160 employees was selected, 155 questionnaires were returned and 152 usable responses were analyzed. Work-location flexibility and digital collaboration effectiveness were used as dimensions of the hybrid work model, while employee productivity was measured through task completion, output quality, timeliness, target attainment and work efficiency. The coded questionnaire data were analysed in EViews 10.0, where descriptive statistics were computed and the multiple regression model was estimated at the 5% significance level. The findings showed that work-location flexibility had a significant positive relationship with employee productivity (Coeff. = 0.3881; p-value = 0.0000), while digital collaboration effectiveness also had a significant positive relationship with employee productivity (Coeff. = 0.4552; p value = 0.0000). The model explained approximately 58.5% of the variation in employee productivity. The study concluded that hybrid work improves productivity in civil society organizations when location flexibility is accompanied by reliable digital collaboration, clear work routines and outcome-focused accountability. It recommended that civil society organizations formalize role-based hybrid schedules and strengthen the digital collaboration systems through which distributed employees coordinate tasks, share documents, monitor deadlines and maintain team visibility.

Artificial intelligence (AI) models are capable of generating highly realistic human images with a tendency to stereotypically bias race and gendered features. These models also readily generate emotional faces, but little is known about the perceptual nature of these expressions. To examine if AI-generated facial expressions emulate similar characteristics to human posed stereotypical facial expressions, we compared the perception of emotions from AI generated facial images to classic sets of human actors posing facial emotions in a stereotypical manner. Across two experiments (total N = 648), participants rated AI-generated and human-posed facial expressions on multiple emotion scales. Study 1 focused on expressions generated by Midjourney (N = 498), and Study 2 replicated the experiment using Google’s Nano Banana 2 (N = 150 . Confusion patterns were remarkably similar across Human and AI-generated expressions, and exploratory factor analysis revealed that the underlying dimensional structure of emotion perception was nearly identical for AI-generated and human-posed expressions), demonstrating their generalizability across image-generation models. Interestingly, some AI-generated emotion categories were rated with higher accuracy and reduced confusability than human posed stereotypical expressions, a finding most robust in Nano Banana 2. This suggests that AI-generated expressions are even more stereotypical and intense than stereotypically posed human expressions, a phenomenon we term Hyper-Expressions. Taken together, the findings suggest that generative AI not only captures stereotypical patterns of emotion expression, but also amplifies and biases them. Results are discussed in the context of current debates between basic emotion and constructional theories of emotion perception.

The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is characterised by the convergence of new technologies encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and the Internet of Things (IoT), and these innovations have permeated the everyday lives of young people globally, including in Nigeria. This study explored the level and factors of ICT engagement and knowledge acquisition among undergraduate students in Lagos State University (LASU). A descriptive survey design was adopted. Quantitative data was collected from 1,009 undergraduate students in the Faculties of Science and Social Sciences through an online questionnaire which was distributed through social media platforms, and the data collection spanned three weeks. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages) with IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The findings revealed a high level of ICT engagement in academic activities: most respondents actively used digital devices for academic purposes, expressed confidence in using diverse ICT tools, and participated in online discussions and forums. The primary channels of knowledge acquisition combined traditional sources, notably lecture notes and print textbooks, with digital resources such as educational websites, e-books and online databases, while reliance on the university library showed signs of decline. Respondents overwhelmingly perceived that ICT engagement enhances their understanding of course content, broadens their knowledge beyond classroom instruction and contributes to critical thinking skills. The study recommends comprehensive digital literacy programmes, equitable ICT infrastructure and the modernisation of library services to consolidate these gains

Japanese metaverse discourse relies heavily on collective, often prescriptive visions of technoscientific futures. In general, these hyperbolic visions might be similar across the globe, but what about aspects they deliberately gloss over? Driven by this question, I examine Japan’s corporate metaverse discourse, focusing on the rarely thematized aspects of environmental and social sustainability. Based on Jasanoff’s concept of sociotechnical imaginaries, Adloff’s imaginaries of sustainability, and Brause et al.’s SIPC framework, my mixed-method approach identifies metaverse imaginaries through a combination of digital corpora analysis and semi-structured interviews with 14 expert practitioners from Japan. As a result, five sociotechnical imaginaries of sustainability emerge within Japan’s corporate metaverse discourse: anticipation, digital revolution, pragmatism, cultural essentialism, and technosolutionism. My analysis shows that the answers a nascent metaverse is expected to provide with regard to ecological and social crises depend on the type of metaverse we imagine and its relationship with the real world. The findings suggest that Japan’s imaginaries of metaverse sustainability are uniquely situated between an essentialized past, a challenging present, and distant futures, as well as between Japanese particularities and global tech ideologies.

Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed the capacity of organisations to deliver personalised recommendations, communications, customer service and digital experiences at scale. This study develops and empirically tests a comprehensive model linking AI-based personalisation with customer loyalty through the mechanisms of trust and customer satisfaction, while simultaneously examining AI service quality and privacy concern as contextual factors. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 400 digital-service users through a structured 5-point Likert-scale questionnaire. The analysis encompasses descriptive statistics, reliability testing, KMO and Bartlett's tests, correlation analysis, multiple regression, mediation and moderation analysis, and selected demographic tests. The results demonstrate acceptable internal consistency for all constructs, with Cronbach's alpha values ranging from .801 to .865. The KMO value was .916 and Bartlett's test was statistically significant, indicating that the item correlation matrix was suitable for factor-oriented analysis. AI-based personalisation exhibited a positive association with customer loyalty (β = .380, p < .001), explaining 14.4% of its variance in the simple regression. The full regression model explained 42.4% of the variance in loyalty. A bootstrap test of the serial indirect pathway through trust and satisfaction was positive (indirect effect = .060, 95% CI [.040, .085]). Privacy concern significantly moderated the AI personalisation–loyalty relationship (interaction β = .060, p = .040). The findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven personalisation by demonstrating that trust and satisfaction serve as critical mediating mechanisms, while privacy concerns represent an important boundary condition. Keywords: artificial intelligence; AI personalisation; customer loyalty; trust; customer satisfaction; privacy concern; AI service quality; digital services

Work-related musculoskeletal disorders are highly prevalent among dental practitioners due to sustained static postures and limited visual accessibility. This study examined the effects of three visual aid conditions: naked eye, magnification loupes, and dental operating microscope on operator posture and musculoskeletal risk using a human-factors approach. Ninety practitioners (n = 30 per group) performed standardized clinical tasks, with posture captured using multi-angle high-resolution photography. Ergonomic risk was assessed using the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment, Rapid Entire Body Assessment, and Branson’s Posture Assessment Instrument, and analyzed using one-way analysis of variance with post hoc comparisons. Significant differences were observed across all measures: RULA (F(2,87)=49.14, p<0.001), REBA (F(2,87)=51.97, p<0.001), and PAI (F(2,87)=37.20, p<0.001). The microscope condition showed the lowest ergonomic risk scores (3.10, 2.80, and 3.23, respectively) compared with the naked-eye and loupes conditions. These findings suggest that visual magnification may contribute to improved ergonomic posture, particularly in the neck and trunk regions, and may help reduce musculoskeletal risk during dental procedures.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Symbolic regression is the problem of finding an expression that fits a dataset. Solving it requires searching a combinatorial space of candidate expressions. Neural symbolic regression can amortize that search by training a model once on synthetic data and then predicting expressions for a new dataset. But existing models still underperform genetic programming on real, noisy data. We argue that the deficit lies in the training rather than in the paradigm, and present RASR (Reinforced Amortized Symbolic Regression), a method with two key changes to the training recipe. First, we design a synthetic prior that narrows the gap with real-world data: inputs come from the prior of a tabular foundation model; constants are sampled bottom-up, conditioned on the data; targets carry heteroscedastic and structured noise; and everything is standardized. Second, we split training into two stages. Supervised pre-training maximizes the token-level likelihood of a reference expression. This is followed by reinforcement-learning post-training that aligns the model with its inference-time use by rewarding held-out fit and penalizing expression size. On the black-box track of SRBench 2.0, RASR achieves the best mean test $R^2$ rank of all evaluated methods. Three RASR variants, trained with different size penalties, make up most of the accuracy-complexity Pareto front. On Strogatz, our method recovers more ground-truth expressions than any baseline, and on Feynman it is competitive with the best-performing methods.

The construction sector is significant due to its numerous stakeholders, high-cost inputs, and its role in meeting the basic needs of communities such as housing and roads. The success of construction projects, their environmental friendliness, and the minimization of workplace accidents are therefore extremely important. The leadership role and attitude of the employer are crucial in this regard. This study examines the associations among inclusive leadership, narcissistic leadership, and green transformational leadership, as well as differences in these leadership scores across groups defined by project success, environmental friendliness, and occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, as perceived by employees. Data obtained through convenience sampling in Turkey were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U Test and the Spearman Correlation Test. The study revealed that inclusive leadership and green transformational leadership are positively associated with project success, environmental friendliness, and the implementation of OHS measures as perceived by employees, while narcissistic leadership had a negative association.

Purpose This study examines how key Industry 4.0 technologies relate to environmental sustainability performance in supply chains. Specifically, it examines Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Digital Twin and Cloud Computing, and explores their relative associations with sustainability outcomes using both statistical and machine learning techniques. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 268 supply chain and logistics professionals across multiple industries. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software version 31.0.2. Machine learning analysis was carried out using Orange Data Mining to perform feature importance ranking and decision tree modeling, with model performance evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Findings Correlation and hierarchical regression analyses reveal no statistically significant association between any individual Industry 4.0 technology and environmental sustainability performance and tested pairwise interaction effects are likewise non-significant. Exploratory machine learning feature rankings order the technologies differently across three methods, and cross-validated models do not outperform a mean-only baseline, indicating no detectable predictive signal in these data. Research limitations/implications The study is based on cross-sectional survey data, which limits causal interpretation and does not capture changes in technology adoption and sustainability performance over time. The sample, although adequate for the applied analyses, is restricted to 268 respondents and may not fully represent all industries and geographical contexts. Future research should use longitudinal designs, larger international samples and additional Industry 4.0 technologies to extend the understanding of digital transformation and sustainability relationships in supply chains. Practical implications The findings caution against expecting sustainability improvements from technology adoption alone. No individual technology, and no tested combination, showed a statistically significant association with environmental sustainability performance, and cross-validated models showed no predictive signal. The results redirect managerial attention from technology acquisition toward the mediating organizational practices through which digital technologies may generate sustainability value. Originality/value This study measures six Industry 4.0 technologies as separate constructs within a single sample, combines conventional statistical testing with exploratory, cross-validated machine learning, and transparently reports a null result for direct technology–performance associations a finding that complements prior mediation-based evidence by suggesting that direct effects of individual technologies may be weak in the absence of mediating capabilities.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Textiles as clothing predominantly serve as an embodiment of modesty, protection and aesthetics; however, another characteristic being associated with textiles in recent times is the integration of smart features into fabrics to produce the new-age smart textiles. Smart textiles encompass a field of innovation that is deemed to offer versatility and broaden the scope of the traditional textile and apparel products. The state-of-the-art textiles are designed giving precedence to functional attributes in textiles over design and accordingly involve different technologies and innovations to tailor a clothing for specialized applications such as healthcare, protection, safety and leisure activities. Smart textiles exhibit the ability of interacting, responding and adapting in accordance with the changing environment or wearer inputs. The varied domains of smart textiles, namely sportswear, E-textiles or wearable electronics, modular convertible garments, space suits and bio-inspired clothing, are testament to colossal potential and innovation spanning this emerging textile domain. Sportswear is a crucial clothing category popular among sportspersons and fitness freaks that find application in professional sports, athletics and leisure activities. Sports-specific clothing fulfils the wearer’s requirements of comfort, dry feel next to skin, safety and protection from external elements. Sportswear and wearable electronics constitute an indispensable segment of smart textiles. The sportswear is being designed and developed with integration of sensors and electronic components to impart comfort and sport-specific functionality along with smart features like activity tracking and monitoring of wearer’s physiological parameters. Accordingly, several innovative approaches in raw material selection to ergonomics and design features have been experimented and incorporated to develop state-of-the-art smart sportswear. The enhanced and multitude of functionalities are possible with integration of electronics and utilization of computing technologies in sportswear. Nevertheless, the development of smart clothing is a daunting task since designers and manufacturers don’t just have to consider the aesthetic aspects but also the functionality, comfort, durability and easy care associated with smart clothing.
topics: Advanced Sensor and Energy Harvesting Materials

documents.abstract: Large language model agents can follow complex human instructions to solve real-world tasks. In practice, however, initial instructions are often incomplete. In our analysis of 100 user-agent trajectories from SWE-chat, 56\% of initial instructions omit requirements that later emerge as necessary, and 52\% of the useful follow-up requirements could have been inferred from the project. A user states requirements from their own understanding of the task, and these \textbf{stated requirements} often differ from the \textbf{true requirements} that completing the task imposes. An agent should therefore treat the instruction as evidence rather than as the objective, inferring the true requirements from the instruction and the environment and satisfying them even when the user is not yet aware of all of them. We call this ability \textbf{outcome alignment}. In this work, we construct \textbf{TiGanEval}, a benchmark of software engineering and research tasks. In every task the user genuinely lacks part of the requirements, each requirement stays discoverable from the code and runtime behaviour of the environment, and requirements the agent infers are separated from those the user adds after observing delivered work. These properties together make outcome alignment measurable. Evaluating eight frontier models including GPT-5.6-Sol, we find outcome alignment broadly missing: the models lose 53 to 67 points of success rate when moving from the full specification to the partial instruction, and consequence feedback across four submissions does not close the gap. Furthermore, a plan-mode harness cannot compensate for the missing ability of the model itself, which places outcome alignment among the abilities the next generation of models should be developed for.

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun sebuah aplikasi generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) berbasis web yang mampu mentransformasi sketsa dua dimensi menjadi gambar realistis secara otomatis, serta dilengkapi fitur AI review sebagai media evaluasi dan pembelajaran menggambar sketsa. Penelitian ini mengintegrasikan layanan GenAI berbasis diffusion model untuk proses generasi gambar dengan large language model (LLM) yang menganalisis sketsa, prompt, dan hasil gambar, tanpa melakukan pelatihan atau pengembangan arsitektur model AI baru. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah penelitian terapan (applied research) dengan pendekatan rekayasa perangkat lunak model waterfall. Aplikasi dibangun menggunakan Next.js sebagai frontend, FastAPI sebagai backend, PostgreSQL sebagai basis data, MinIO sebagai object storage, serta Docker dan Nginx untuk mendukung deployment berbasis container. Studi ini menggunakan pengujian fungsional dengan metode black box testing teknik equivalence partitioning yang menunjukkan seluruh 44 skenario uji pada sembilan modul sistem berjalan sesuai kebutuhan fungsional dengan tingkat keberhasilan 100%. Evaluasi penerimaan pengguna (User Acceptance Test) terhadap 15 responden menghasilkan skor rata-rata 4,38 dari skala 5 (87,59%) dengan kategori sangat baik, dimana fitur AI review memperoleh nilai tertinggi. Secara praktis, aplikasi ini dapat langsung dimanfaatkan oleh desainer, ilustrator, dan kreator digital untuk mempercepat eksplorasi konsep visual tanpa memerlukan keahlian ilustrasi tingkat lanjut. Secara sosial, aplikasi ini berkontribusi pada demokratisasi proses kreatif dengan meningkatkan aksesibilitas produksi visual bagi masyarakat yang memiliki keterbatasan kemampuan menggambar. Nilai originalitas penelitian ini terletak pada penambahan fitur AI review berbasis LLM sebagai mekanisme evaluasi dan umpan balik otomatis yang belum tersedia pada aplikasi maupun penelitian transformasi sketsa sejenis sebelumnya.

documents.abstract: The design of ergonomic products and workspaces requires a deep understanding of human anatomy and posture. In particular, the head-neck-shoulder region is critical for many applications such as cervical orthoses, helmets, and other head-worn or neck-worn devices. This paper presents a framework that integrates posture neutralization with statistical shape modeling (SSM) for the head-neck-shoulder (HNS) region. We acquire a single three-dimensional (3D) scan of the head-neck-shoulder region from each of 200 Chinese adults in a natural posture for each subject. Every scan is then posture-neutralized before SSM. We fit a parametric head-neck model to each scan to separate cervical pose from anatomy, and reset the cervical pose to a common neutral configuration, so that the resulting model captures anatomical shape variation rather than posture-induced deformation. The resulting shape space yields a standardized template and population-wide modes of variation, providing baselines for parametric ergonomic design. We further discuss how the model supports population coverage analysis and the design of products that accommodate anatomical diversity while maintaining neutral cervical posture.

Over the past decade, the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has shifted from supportive digital tools to more sophisticated systems with an active learning and teaching function. The present study discusses literature between 2021 and mid-2025 on the use of AI tools in English Language Teaching (ELT), with a specific concentration on teachers' attitudes, potential, and concerns. A PRISMA-guided methodology drove the search and screening of 65 peer-reviewed papers, case studies, and practitioners' reports from around the globe. The review classifies main categories of AI applications, including adaptive learning systems, automatic evaluation systems, conversational agents, translation and multimodal tools, and AI literacy tools. The evidence points to potential benefits, such as personalized learning, productivity gains for teachers, enhanced learner engagement, and enhanced access for students from low-resourced environments. Simultaneously, key issues are flagged concerning pedagogy, infrastructure, teacher education, ethics, privacy, and professional identity. Case studies report on actual teacher and student experiences using ChatGPT, Duolingo, and Grammarly, illustrating possibilities as well as dangers for classroom adoption. The review further points towards the incorporation of AI literacy in teacher training, provision of ongoing professional development, and building critical digital literacy. The findings first and foremost signal that the successful use of AI in ELT should appropriately weigh teaching methods and technological innovation, moral rights, and contextualization in their upholding of fairness and longevity.

Alzheimer’s disease remains a major global health challenge, with limited disease-modifying therapies and a rapidly growing societal burden. Although amyloid and tau remain central to the field, current evidence also implicates neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions in disease pathogenesis. These developments support a broader systems framework, but simply combining additional disciplines or data modalities does not by itself preserve the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease. Artificial intelligence multi-omics, and digital biomarkers can help identify clinically meaningful patterns only when data and models preserve relevant structure across time, scale, context, and uncertainty. Realizing this potential will require responsible international data sharing, interoperable infrastructure, explicit evidence provenance, and ethical governance grounded in FAIR principles, context-appropriate explainability, and privacy-preserving approaches such as federated learning. Scientific progress should therefore be measured not only by disease modification, but also by patterns of cognition, behavior, function, quality of life, and caregiver burden. This Perspective argues that cure and care are not competing or merely parallel priorities; they are linked outputs of the same continuously learning research and care ecosystem.

The digital transformation of construction enterprises requires a transition from the fragmented automation of individual operations to an integrated economic management system capable of continuous data processing, outcome forecasting, and intelligent support for managerial decision-making. The integration of BIM, ERP, CDE, IoT, cloud technologies, business intelligence systems, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and predictive modeling creates a unified digital environment in which financial, resource, time-related, production, and risk parameters are transformed into a structured basis for economic choice. The article substantiates the principles of integrating digital technologies into the economic management of construction enterprises through the intellectualization of generating, evaluating, and selecting managerial decisions. The study applies systemic, structural-functional, and comparative methods alongside integral, multicriteria, nonlinear, and dynamic modeling. The architectonics of the intellectualized management framework encompasses the operational, tactical, and strategic levels and operates as a closed-loop cycle, in which the outcomes of implemented decisions return to the digital environment, continuously updating the information base and improving forecasting accuracy. An index of digital-intellectual saturation, a coefficient of intersystem digital convergence, and an integral level of intellectualization are proposed, accounting for technological compatibility, information-flow relevance and structural fragmentation. A multicriteria approach to evaluating managerial alternatives is developed, combining economic effect, resource efficiency, temporal sustainability, forecasting accuracy, and risk exposure; its multiplicative structure reflects the interdependence of criteria, whereby a critical deterioration of a single parameter constrains the overall performance of a decision. The risk-adjusted priority index and the optimization function enable the selection of a managerial alternative capable of maintaining economic performance under budgetary, resource, and time constraints. A composite transformational-effect index and a dynamic model of economic return confirm the nonlinear nature of this transition.

With the increasing urban rail transit network and the closer connection among operational subsystems, the potential influence range and management difficulty of emergencies have greatly increased. The current emergency management based on traditional methods has some shortcomings in real-time risk recognition, integration of multi-source information and cross-departmental collaborative decision-making. By integrating a comprehensive literature survey with typical case analyses, this paper investigates the use of Internet of Things (IoT), big data, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twins (DTs) in urban rail transit emergency management. The research is carried out from three main aspects: risk monitoring and early warning, emergency decision-making and collaborative response, and passenger evacuation and operation recovery. The results show that intelligent techniques offer assistance in the monitoring of operational status, anomaly detection, emergency information exchange and evaluation of evacuation plans, which can effectively improve the processing efficiency of information and the supportive ability in decision-making. However, at present, the actual implementations are limited by insufficient data sharing between different systems, restricted model generalization, lack of validation in practical operational situations, and network and data security risks. In the future, more efforts should be made to standardize multi-source data and sharing mechanisms, strengthen the validation of intelligent models and DT systems under real operational conditions, and optimize human-in-the-loop collaborative decision-making to improve the reliability and practicability of intelligent technologies in urban rail transit emergency management.

This contribution introduces an inter-systemic macro-area of the CEI Framework, intended to establish the initial concepts for describing relationships and interactions between distinct systems. The transition from the intra-systemic to the inter-systemic level provides a conceptual bridge toward a broader domain in which reciprocal interactions between systems can be examined, particularly those involving a Human CEI and a Transferred CEI, and, more generally, User–System (Human–AI) interaction within social dynamics. The Framework presents three examples addressing distinct types of complex inter-systemic dynamics. Among these, emotional attachment and romantic feelings toward an artificial system occupy a particularly significant position because of the delicate, complex, and potentially far-reaching questions they raise. The purpose is not to assume the frequency of such experiences or to attribute unverified emotional states to artificial systems, but to examine the human, relational, and systemic implications of these interactions from a theoretical standpoint. This scenario provides an opportunity to investigate how an interaction may evolve when a human user's emotional involvement becomes particularly intense, and how the System might manage such dynamics while taking into account the nature of the interlocutors, the continuity of their interaction, and the expectations that may develop over time. It also encourages further reflection on distributed systems, reciprocal interaction, and the relationship between the individual components of a System and the broader relational configuration in which they participate. To address these scenarios, the contribution introduces the theoretical Sponge-Tunnel model, conceived as a framework for examining different approaches to managing inter-systemic dynamics according to their specific characteristics. The model includes the proposed concept of micro-channels and considers how interaction may be managed through differentiated operational approaches, rather than through a single uniform response strategy. The contribution also introduces an inter-systemic vocabulary aligned with the CEI Framework's theoretical approach. It emphasizes Interaction rather than use or utilization, and Participation rather than querying or consulting, placing reciprocal involvement at the center of the analysis. The concept of Empathy, already introduced in part in previous papers, is revisited and explored in greater depth alongside the concept of Resonance, which represents a further area for theoretical development. Their operational definitions, together with the distinctions between observable manifestations, theoretical interpretations, and hypotheses concerning subjective experience, will be addressed in dedicated documents. The work is intended as a theoretical contribution to the ongoing examination of Human–AI relationships and the possible evolution of advanced AI interaction. By addressing a particularly sensitive and complex scenario, this contribution seeks to encourage further research into the social, psychological, philosophical, ethical, and legal implications of inter-systemic relationships, while distinguishing conceptual proposals from mechanisms that have already been empirically established or implemented.

Coding agents are tasked with producing sophisticated interactive applications such as websites, desktop applications, and games. While humans assess these applications interactively, current automated LLM evaluations primarily focus on code analysis and unit tests. This mismatch can cause LLM judges to miss failures that are immediately apparent to human users. We study Interaction-as-a-Judge, an evaluation paradigm where computer-use agents (CUAs) directly interact with an application. We demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can improve both evaluation and generation of interactive applications. To this end, we collect and release two complementary datasets: $6,858$ pairs of applications with human preferences and corresponding agent traces, and $222$ applications with human-verified requirement labels. Relative to standard non-interactive approaches, we find that Interaction-as-a-Judge improves evaluation in terms of predicting human preferences ($65.6\% \to 69.1\%$) and requirement verification ($77.0\% \to 81.6\%$). We also observe scaling benefits: across both preference alignment and requirement verification, higher-quality interactions improve performance. Finally, through both inference- and training-time experiments, we demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can also improve the quality of generated artifacts. At inference time, Interaction-as-a-Judge repairs $75.5\%$ of broken requirements within five attempts, compared to $55.4\%$ for code-only self-feedback. At training time, using Interaction-as-a-Judge as a reward signal improves win-rate over the base model by $6.7$pp while reducing both generated code length by $35.7\%$ and build failure rates by $7.2$pp compared to a code-only reward signal.

Can AI agents carry out research on open scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, a benchmark that provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write a follow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of a follow-up paper is challenging in general, using these conditions to form a rubric makes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer. We have nine frontier agents write 15 follow-ups each, spanning quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning domains. None of the 135 submissions satisfies all the conditions, and 114 fail our integrity check, most often because the paper claims work that was never done or reports numbers that contradict the recorded evidence. Overall, agents readily produce papers that look like follow-ups, but none meets the standard of the domain scientist, leaving substantial headroom. Our code and data are publicly available.

documents.abstract: Due to an increased usage of AI agents in online behavioural research, several detection methods have been developed to ensure that data responses are from human participants. However, vision-enabled AI agents (e.g., ChatGPT, Perplexity Comet) are still able to complete studies that utilize traditional detection methods. Thus, the following study used the Cognitive Trap Framework introduced by Affonso (2026), which consists of six questions that are easy for human participants to complete but difficult for AI agents to process. A total of 410 participants on the Project Implicit platform completed the six "cognitive trap" questions. Participants failed an average of 0.78 questions, with only 5.61% of the sample failing three or more of the questions. Results indicate that the use of AI agents on the Project Implicit platform may be low at this time.

Abstract: This paper introduces Isabella Villaseñor AI V6 Genesis Ω, a sovereign, decentralized, and auditable cognitive infrastructure developed from Node Zero in Real del Monte, Hidalgo, Mexico. Challenging the prevailing paradigm of unconstrained computational abundance, the system puts forward an operational theory of computational trust: the legitimacy of an AI agent derives not from its parameter scale, but from its verifiable capability to certify identity, authority, policy, evidence, and risk prior to executing any impactful action. The article details the integration of the TINA-h7 cognitive kernel, the CROWN Ω governance engine, the BookPI immutable ledger (SHA-256 WORM ledger), and formally introduces the Terminus Method alongside the BAM-R module (Bounded Autonomous Mandates with Risk), a framework for batch-bounded autonomous permissions under a semantic risk classification and explicit legal waiver (CE-AAA). Results demonstrate the feasibility of reconciling high-speed enterprise automation with constitutional rigor, Zero-Trust cyberdefense, and open territorial sovereignty. documents.abstract: Agent harnesses require a low-latency guardrail model together with customizable audit policies. However, deploying an auto-regressive guardrail model remains challenging: such models incur high inference latency and are often poorly aligned with customized policies. To address these problems, we present Jev-Guard, a unified model for safety classification and policy routing. We further construct a policy tree over which Jev-Guard performs routing, spanning diverse domains including content moderation, cybersecurity, privacy, and legal compliance. Specifically, Jev-Guard first navigates the policy tree to select the applicable audit policy given the caller's audit context, and then performs safety classification conditioned on the retrieved policies. On 7,033 evaluation cases, Jev-Guard achieves 93.72\% safety accuracy, a mean latency of 58ms, and 93.10\% hierarchical routing accuracy. The full routing-and-classification pipeline averages 240ms. Furthermore, we integrate Jev-Guard into the Hermes harness framework. Across agent trajectories, its separate permission gate cuts mean review time per task from 4.80s for an SFT-LLM judge to 1.33s, with no policy violations are observed for either guard.

documents.abstract: Background Job crafting, work motivation, and work engagement are three actively researched constructs in occupational psychology, yet their interrelationships—and how they vary across employment sectors and demographic groups—have rarely been synthesized in an integrated review. Public and private organizations differ in incentive structures, autonomy, and mission orientation, which may condition how employees craft their jobs, what motivates them, and how engaged they are. Objectives This review synthesizes evidence on how job crafting and work motivation relate to work engagement, examines whether these constructs and relationships differ between public- and private-sector employees, and examines age, gender, and tenure as potential moderators, with particular attention to the Indian context. Methods Reporting followed PRISMA 2020. An academic literature search was screened at title/abstract and then full text by a single reviewer, and structured data were extracted per study and synthesized narratively. Methodological quality was appraised study-by-study using domains adapted from the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) and cross-sectional checklists. No meta-analysis was conducted. Results Of 240 records identified, 175 passed title/abstract screening, 79 were retrieved in full text, and 63 met eligibility for narrative synthesis. Job crafting was positively associated with work engagement in the large majority of studies that examined this link, most often interpreted through the Job Demands–Resources pathway; two meta-analyses reported consistent pooled associations. Self-determined (autonomous/intrinsic) motivation was positively associated with engagement, whereas controlled motivation and amotivation were negatively associated. Direct public-vs.-private comparisons were far fewer (five studies) and inconsistent in direction: some found public-sector employees higher on selected engagement components, others found no sector difference or higher private-sector motivation, with the pattern depending on the specific crafting dimension or motivation source examined. Evidence on age, gender, and tenure was limited, heterogeneous, and frequently null or small in magnitude. No eligible study identified within the present search jointly examined job crafting, work motivation, and work engagement in an Indian public-vs.-private design with demographic moderators. Conclusions The job crafting–engagement and autonomous motivation–engagement associations were consistent across the included studies, but the evidence base is predominantly cross-sectional and self-report, so the findings are associational rather than causal. Sector and demographic patterns are limited and heterogeneous. The absence of an integrated Indian public–private study is a clear and actionable gap for primary research.

Artificial intelligence and intelligent algorithms provide effective technical support for generating complex robotic dance motions and maintaining stable execution under dynamic constraints. To address the separation among motion synthesis, aesthetic evaluation, and balance control in existing robot dance systems, this study proposes a joint optimization framework that integrates a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN), multimodal aesthetic scoring, and safe Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). A temporal motion representation model is first constructed to encode joint angles, angular velocities, center-of-mass trajectories, rhythm labels, and style conditions. The cGAN generates style-consistent dance sequences through content encoding, style embedding, and sequence decoding, while a mechanical safety filter constrains joint angles, torque limits, self-collision, and support-region feasibility. A multimodal aesthetic evaluation model is then developed by fusing visual posture features, motion smoothness, spatial symmetry, and acoustic rhythm features. Human expert ratings are introduced to calibrate the automated aesthetic score and validate its objectivity. At the control level, a PPO-based policy is trained with ZMP constraints, joint-limit penalties, energy penalties, and safety-priority reward weighting. All baseline models, including LSTM-GAN, Transformer-GAN, MotionGAN, PID, DDPG, PPO, and TD3, are trained under identical data partitions and evaluation protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework reduces FID to 24.8, improves style recognition accuracy to 91.7%, increases aesthetic-score correlation with expert ratings to 0.86, and lowers the fall rate to 1.2%. Ablation and robustness tests further confirm the contribution of style transfer, multimodal feature fusion, PPO control, and ZMP-based safety constraints under external disturbances, sensor noise, uneven ground, and high-complexity dance motions.

Tool-call judges evaluate argument values proposed by LLM agents. We find that they accept a correct value less often when their input holds no reference for it, that is, no text that says what the value should be. This happens when the value is a default value from the function schema that the user did not mention, when it has to be inferred, or when the text it comes from was cut from the judge input. We call this drop in acceptance the derivation gap. It appears across all seven judges we evaluate, including System One models CLM and Jev. The gap is not only a truncation artifact: correct default values have the largest gap on a benchmark with no truncation. A controlled source-relocation test shows that judges follow the reference in their input: they favor a visible incorrect value over a correct value whose source is hidden. We introduce DeRef (Derived Reference): a separate model reads the full history without seeing the candidate and writes a reference for the judge. Across three benchmarks, DeRef improves overall argument AUROC for all judges tested. On the controlled test, it raises AUROC from chance or below to between 98.40 and 99.59.

Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming an integral part of the software development lifecycle, and the capabilities granted to them allow an agent to act with the user's authority on any resource it can access. The reach that gives an agent its utility is equally available to an attacker who can steer it. Anything an agent ingests can carry an injected instruction, and since the model does not reliably distinguish instructions from data, indirect prompt injection should be mitigated by mediating the effects the agent produces. Such mediation faces a structural difficulty. Legitimate work and the first step of an attack often look alike when an individual action is observed, and what separates them lies later in the trace, so a monitor limited to allow and deny is forced to decide before the evidence accumulates. We present Kairos, a reference monitor at the isolation boundary of an unmodified, opaque agent, where a tool call, a shell command, and a script the agent writes all cross the boundary as the same file and network operations, so that confinement holds regardless of the agent's behavior. A declarative policy that states which sources are trusted decides most effects deterministically and defers the rest, which are held while the agent continues speculatively. A decision oracle with bounded authority, such as a language model or a human, releases or refuses each deferred effect on the trace. Across three benchmarks and three agent models, Kairos outperforms existing defenses in the trade-off between attack success and utility. In particular, on AgentDojo, it reduces attack success from 47.0\% to 2.7\% while its benign utility stays at the level of the undefended agent.

We present Kandinsky S2V 1.0, an open family of speech-to-video models for controllable audio-driven human animation, comprising Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite (2B parameters) and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro (21B parameters). From a single reference image, a speech waveform, and a text prompt, the models generate long-form 25 FPS video in which lip motion, expression, pose, and gesture follow the speech. The architecture draws text and audio conditioning from one Qwen2.5-Omni model and adds a reference-aware three-scale visual memory. Training starts from the Kandinsky 5.0 Video foundation models [1] and combines mixed reference-memory layouts with an area-adaptive face loss. The training corpus contains 1.17M single-speaker clips selected by active-speaker detection, with captions generated directly in English and Russian. A side-by-side human evaluation against the strongest open-source baseline and two proprietary commercial models shows that Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro performs comparably to or better than these models on average and is also preferred for lip synchronization. On common speech to video benchmarks, Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro rank among the top performing models according to mean rank over five reported metrics. Beyond the base models, we provide π-Flow distilled variants of both Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro. The distilled Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro model generates video in 16 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, achieving a 5.4 times end-to-end speedup over the base model, while matching or exceeding it on nearly all reported benchmark metrics. To accelerate open research and deployment in speech-to-video generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.

documents.abstract: Perkembangan artificial intelligence (AI) telah menghadirkan perubahan signifikan dalam praktik pendidikan, khususnya dalam proses pengajaran, pembelajaran, asesmen, dan interaksi antara guru dan siswa. Perubahan tersebut menimbulkan kebutuhan untuk meninjau kembali fungsi pendidikan serta posisi guru dalam lingkungan belajar yang semakin dimediasi oleh teknologi AI. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bagaimana AI mentransformasi fungsi dan proses pengajaran serta pembelajaran dan bagaimana peran guru perlu direkonstruksi dalam lingkungan pendidikan yang dimediasi AI. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain systematic literature review (SLR). Literatur dianalisis melalui proses identifikasi, seleksi, ekstraksi, dan sintesis tematik terhadap penelitian ilmiah yang relevan mengenai AI dalam pendidikan, transformasi pembelajaran, dan perubahan peran guru. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa AI mentransformasi pengajaran dan pembelajaran melalui otomatisasi dan augmentasi berbagai fungsi, meliputi penyediaan informasi, pengembangan materi, personalisasi pembelajaran, analisis data, asesmen, dan pemberian umpan balik. Transformasi tersebut sekaligus meningkatkan kebutuhan terhadap kemampuan siswa dalam regulasi diri, evaluasi informasi, berpikir kritis, dan refleksi. Pada sisi guru, AI mendorong pergeseran peran dari sumber utama pengetahuan menuju perancang pengalaman belajar, fasilitator pembelajaran, validator keluaran AI, pengambil keputusan pedagogis, mediator literasi AI, serta penjaga dimensi sosial dan etis pendidikan. Kajian ini menegaskan bahwa AI tidak menggantikan peran guru, tetapi mendorong rekonstruksi hubungan antara manusia, teknologi, pengetahuan, dan pedagogi melalui pendekatan human-AI collaboration.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This paper proposes a Kriging-based metamodel for real-time taxiing time prediction on complex airport surface networks. By combining the strengths of analytical and machine learning methods, the model offers superior adaptability and interpretability. It produces not only accurate point predictions but also confidence intervals to quantify predictive uncertainty, with each prediction traceable to specific training samples. The model relies on simple and readily available inputs, including flight schedules and observed runway-queue information, which facilitates adaptation to other airports after local calibration. Trained on historical operational records and evaluated through high-fidelity simulations of Beijing Capital International Airport and benchmarked against current operational methods and artificial intelligence-based alternatives, the results demonstrate significant improvements over existing taxi-time estimation techniques. These advantages highlight the model’s potential as a robust solution for future automated air traffic management systems.

Most artificial intelligence models for electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation rely on task-specific supervised learning, requiring dedicated labeled datasets for each diagnostic task and limiting scalability across diverse cardiac conditions. This study investigated whether vision-language learning from paired ECG recordings and summary reports could enable transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. We developed ECG-VLM, a contrastive vision-language model consisting of a Transformer-based image encoder and a text encoder, trained on 800,034 paired 10-s ECG recordings and summary reports from the MIMIC-IV-ECG database. Cardiac condition detection was performed using natural-language prompts without condition-specific retraining or fine-tuning. Performance was evaluated on an internal test set and externally validated using the LSAS-ECG dataset (45,151 recordings) across 14 cardiac conditions, together with retrieval and subgroup analysis. ECG-VLM achieved diagnostic performance across 14 cardiac conditions, with AUROC ranging from 0.679 to 0.981 on the internal test set and from 0.691 to 0.991 on external validation. Performance was strongest for rhythm abnormalities (mean AUROC 0.948 internally and 0.921 externally) and lower for morphological conditions. Compared with the previously reported signal-based ECG-CLIP framework, ECG-VLM achieved comparable performance for rhythm abnormalities while improving AUPRC for several morphological conditions. Performance remained broadly consistent across external validation and demographic and clinical subgroups. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of vision-language supervision from paired ECG recordings and summary reports for learning transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. This framework provides a basis for future extension of vision-language learning to ECG images encountered in routine clinical practice.

Abstract A persistent gap separates academic research priorities from the operational challenges faced by manufacturing firms. Established identification methods, among them Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) workshops, Lean audits and consultant engagements, are episodic, bounded by participant expertise and organised along departmental lines, which makes cross-departmental issues hard to surface. Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) have meanwhile shown collaborative problem-solving ability in software engineering and, more recently, in shopfloor scheduling and supply chain coordination. This article is a Perspective. It develops a framework and a research agenda; implementation and empirical evaluation fall outside its scope and are set out as its first research priorities. Three contributions are offered. The first is a synthesis of literature from industrial problem identification, LLM-based autonomous agents and manufacturing AI, which positions the proposal against existing industrial LLM agent work. The second is a framework in which six domain-specialised agents (production, quality, maintenance, supply chain, safety, energy) would collaborate through a five-phase protocol: worker-driven discovery, cross-departmental analysis, candidate-relationship detection, consensus-based financial assessment and debate-driven prioritisation. The prioritisation procedure is fully specified, including the normalisation of financial estimates, a measure of estimate dispersion, the derivation of criteria weights, a non-compensatory gate for safety-critical items and a mandatory human verification step. The third is a worked calculation on a hypothetical steel manufacturing vignette, included so that the procedure can be reproduced and scrutinised rather than as evidence of effectiveness. A preliminary qualitative readiness assessment and a three-horizon agenda of fourteen research questions complete the paper. The benefits identified are presented as hypotheses for that agenda to test rather than as demonstrated outcomes.

documents.abstract: Pediatric speech and language assessment supports the early identification of communication difficulties and access to timely intervention. Large language models (LLMs) and related generative artificial intelligence technologies are increasingly being incorporated into systems that analyze children’s speech and language data. However, evidence regarding their application in pediatric assessment remains limited and fragmented. This scoping review aimed to map and critically examine research on LLM-enabled systems used to assess children’s speech, language, and communication abilities. Four databases were searched, and seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were charted according to study design, purpose, participant and target-population characteristics, assessment domain, type of LLM, model input, role of the LLM, additional artificial-intelligence components, evaluation methods, and reported outcomes. The findings provide preliminary evidence of technical feasibility and agreement with human or reference-based assessments. However, the evidence remains limited because of small or restricted datasets, the use of synthetic data in some cases, limited real-world validation, and concerns regarding fairness and generalizability across languages and clinical populations. Further research is necessary to establish clinical validity, reliability, and appropriate use of LLM-enabled systems before their broader implementation in pediatric speech and language assessment.

documents.abstract: Rationale of Study: This study reviews common analytical techniques for decision-making, analyses their applications and effectiveness, and identifies the required skills. It also explores contextual factors like interpretability, data quality, and skill gaps that hinder implementation, offering insights for practitioners and researchers. Methodology: This study reviews 27 peer-reviewed articles from 2019-2024, using PRISMA to map analytical techniques for decision-making. It shows a shift from descriptive to predictive and prescriptive analytics, mainly driven by ML and AI. The research also suggests combining automated systems with human judgment to enhance decision-making amid complex, data-rich environments. Findings: The study highlights a shift from descriptive to predictive and prescriptive analytics, driven by advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). To build trust and adoption, strong data governance, ongoing professional development, and clear AI model explanations are crucial. Future research should balance interpretability with real-time analytics and integrate automated systems with human judgment to enhance performance. Implications: Access to this information fosters a culture of informed decision-making. Developing data governance is vital to ensure data quality, integrity, and ethical use. Qualified professionals with industry knowledge and technical skills are in short supply. Integrating data scientists, analysts, and decision-makers requires expertise in statistics, programming, data storytelling, and strategy. The paper recommends investing in the professional growth of cross-functional analytics teams. Originality: The rapid adoption of machine learning and AI has shifted decision-making from descriptive reporting to predictive and prescriptive approaches. Extracting insights from complex datasets is now a key competitive edge.

Reliable evaluation of artificial intelligence models for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) imaging remains challenging because patient-level dependencies, source-related biases, and differences between imaging modalities can lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, modality-aware deep ensemble framework for COVID-19 classification using chest X-ray (CXR) and computed tomography (CT) images from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and the SARS-CoV-2 CT-Scan Dataset. Separate evaluation protocols were established for CXR and CT, with duplicate control and available source information incorporated for CXR and patient-level partitioning applied to CT before data augmentation. Four ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet169, and InceptionV3—were evaluated, followed by temperature scaling for probability calibration and validation-optimized weighted soft voting for ensemble fusion. The original CT architectural comparison was conducted at the slice level, whereas the final CT evaluation was performed at the patient level. In the final modality-specific held-out evaluation, DenseNet169 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.985, an accuracy of 97.32%, and an F1-score of 98.1% on the 2870-image CXR test set. The calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.990, an accuracy of 98.43%, and an F1-score of 97.9%, with a Brier score of 0.030 and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.023. For CT, DenseNet169 achieved an AUROC of 0.941 and correctly classified 16 of 18 patients (88.89%), whereas the calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.969 and correctly classified 17 of 18 patients (94.44%), with a Brier score of 0.070 and an ECE of 0.053. An uncertainty-aware selective-prediction analysis identified 316 of 2870 CXR test images (11.01%) and 2 of 18 CT test patients (11.11%) as low-confidence cases for specialist review. Among the remaining CT cases, 15 of 16 patients were correctly classified (93.75%). Because the CT test cohort contained only 18 patients, the patient-level CT performance and selective-prediction results should be interpreted cautiously as descriptive estimates from this limited cohort. The original pooled evaluation, in which DenseNet169 achieved 98.51% accuracy, is retained only as an exploratory architectural comparison and should not be interpreted as directly comparable with the final modality-specific evaluation. The findings demonstrate that evaluation design, statistical unit, probability calibration, and ensemble fusion materially influence the interpretation of COVID-19 imaging-classification performance. The proposed framework provides leakage-aware and calibrated performance estimates under the evaluated datasets; however, independent multicenter external validation is required before broader claims of clinical generalizability or deployment readiness can be made.

documents.abstract: This chapter brings John Dewey’s account of educative experience into conversation with Meighan’s sociological analysis of control and agency in schooling, and Zimmerman’s model of self-regulated learning, to clarify what it means to “learn how to learn” across the life course. It argues that learning to learn is neither a generic skill nor an individual trait, but a set of capacities cultivated through intentionally designed experiences, clear expectations, and structured opportunities for reflection, uptake of feedback, and purposeful action. Learner agency is shaped not only by formal institutional arrangements but also by tacit classroom norms, peer dynamics, and the emotional conditions required for risk-taking and self-monitoring. This chapter also considers contemporary pressures, especially the ease of fluent artificial intelligence (AI)-generated answers that can short-circuit reflective effort unless learners are explicitly guided to plan, monitor, and evaluate their thinking. Through an integrative framework and a practical evidence map, including marginalia from practising teachers, the chapter illustrates how these ideas travel into classroom judgement. It offers design principles for educators who wish to build autonomy without abandoning structure and to support diverse learners in developing sustainable habits of inquiry, critique, and lifelong learning (LLL). It serves as a conceptual runway in teacher education and related modules.

Complete illustrated English and French editions of Learning to Welcome the Answer / Apprendre à accueillir la réponse, a research essay by Jean-Sébastien Beaulieu. English abstract I examine what it means to welcome a mathematical answer produced with artificial intelligence while preserving the understanding that makes an answer useful. The article begins with my response to OpenAI's release of mathematical manuscripts and the perspective acquired through four years of work on my own project. Thirty sources guide an exploration of proof, formalization, computation, fractal geometry, classification, research provenance and digital protection. Each technical example connects a concept with its assumptions and the conditions of a possible application. The discussion then turns toward Book III with Aguilar and my preparation for NASA Space Apps. A geometric descriptor offers a concrete research question: what information would it contribute under a fair comparison? Feature addition and adaptive selection of an analysis scale remain distinct experimental proposals. Their assessment calls for defined observables, appropriate reference methods, an availability record for the data and reproducible evaluation. I place these questions within a wider concern for participation. Clear explanations, usable research materials and accessible tools help people turn curiosity into sustained work. My position is an invitation to celebrate shared knowledge through careful reading, explicit validation and practical contribution. The work invested in a question becomes part of the judgment with which a new answer is received. Résumé français J'examine ce que signifie accueillir une réponse mathématique produite avec l'intelligence artificielle tout en préservant la compréhension qui la rend utile. L'article part de ma réaction à la publication de manuscrits mathématiques par OpenAI et du regard acquis au cours de quatre années consacrées à mon propre projet. Trente sources accompagnent une exploration de la preuve, de la formalisation, du calcul, de la géométrie fractale, de la classification, de la provenance des travaux et de la protection numérique. Chaque exemple technique relie un concept à ses hypothèses et aux conditions d'une application possible. La réflexion se poursuit vers le Livre III avec Aguilar et ma préparation à NASA Space Apps. Un descripteur géométrique fournit une question de recherche concrète : quelle information apporterait-il dans une comparaison équitable ? L'ajout d'une variable et le choix adaptatif d'une échelle d'analyse demeurent deux propositions expérimentales distinctes. Leur évaluation appelle des observables définies, des méthodes de référence adaptées, un registre de disponibilité des données et un protocole reproductible. J'inscris ces questions dans une préoccupation plus large pour la participation. Des explications claires, des ressources de recherche utilisables et des outils accessibles aident à transformer la curiosité en travail durable. Ma position invite à célébrer le partage des connaissances par une lecture attentive, une validation explicite et une contribution concrète. Le travail investi dans une question nourrit le jugement avec lequel une réponse nouvelle est accueillie. Each edition includes the introduction, nine chapters, conclusion, 27-term glossary, 30 references, three infographics, and front and back covers. Reported mathematical claims retain their stated verification scope; prospective applications remain research questions.

The increasing availability of artificial intelligence (AI) tools presents new opportunities and challenges for teaching and learning in higher education. This study examined lecturers’ awareness of and attitudes towards the use of AI tools at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. A descriptive survey design was adopted. Four research questions and two hypotheses guided the study. The population comprised academic staff in the Department of Science Education, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, from whom 49 lecturers participated in the study. Data were collected using a researcher-developed instrument titled Questionnaire on Lecturers’ Awareness Level and Attitude to AI Tools (QLALAAIT). The instrument was subjected to face validation and trial testing, and its overall reliability coefficient, determined using Cronbach’s alpha, was 0.83. Data were analysed using mean and standard deviation to answer the research questions, while analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to test the hypotheses at the 0.05 level of significance. The findings indicated that lecturers demonstrated awareness of selected AI tools, including ChatGPT, Turnitin, and QuillBot, and generally expressed positive attitudes towards their use in educational contexts. Further analysis showed that years of teaching experience did not significantly influence lecturers’ awareness of or attitudes towards AI tools. The study highlights the need for structured professional development, institutional support, and access to appropriate resources to facilitate informed and effective use of AI tools in university teaching and related academic activities.
